faqs.question: How many ml are in a US cup?

faqs.answer: A US cup is 236.588 ml. A metric cup is 250 ml, about 6 percent larger. Australian and many international recipes use the metric cup, so check the source.

howToSteps.name: Check which cup the recipe means
howToSteps.text: An American recipe means the US cup, 236.588 ml. A recipe from Australia or an international site may mean the metric cup, 250 ml. Check the source before converting.

howToSteps.name: Multiply by 236.588
howToSteps.text: Cups times 236.588 gives milliliters. Half a cup is 118 ml, a full cup is 237 ml, two cups is 473 ml.

howToSteps.name: Read the rounded result
howToSteps.text: Results show one decimal below 100 ml and whole milliliters above that. The rounding is smaller than the error in any measuring jug.

howToSteps.name: Measure liquids at eye level
howToSteps.text: Put the jug on the counter and read the meniscus at eye level. Reading from above makes the level look lower than it is.

name: Cups to Milliliters
title: US Cups to Milliliters Converter
tutorial: One US cup is 236.588 milliliters. The number is exact, not rounded: a US gallon is defined as 231 cubic inches, which is exactly 3.785411784 liters, and a cup is one sixteenth of a gallon. Divide 3785.411784 by 16 and you get 236.588. That is the number this converter uses.

The metric cup is the trap. A metric cup is 250 ml, about 6 percent larger than a US cup. Recipes from Australia and many international sites use the metric cup, so a recipe that says 2 cups may mean 500 ml, not 473 ml. If the recipe is in grams and milliliters alongside cups, it is probably metric. If it is in cups and Fahrenheit, it is American.

The 240 ml shortcut shows up on American nutrition labels, where a cup is rounded to 240 ml for simplicity. It overshoots the true cup by about 1.4 percent, which is fine for a smoothie and not fine for a cake. For baking, use 236.588, or better, weigh the ingredient.

Milliliter results on this page show one decimal below 100 ml and round to whole milliliters above that, so 1 cup shows as 237 ml and 2 cups as 473 ml. The rounding is smaller than the error in any measuring jug, so it never changes a recipe. The exact factor, 236.588, is in the formula below.

A kitchen scale beats both units for baking. Cups measure volume, and a cup of flour can weigh anywhere from 120 to 150 grams depending on how it is scooped. Milliliters have the same problem for dry ingredients. For liquids, milliliters are exact, and a jug with ml markings is the most accurate way to measure them.
